messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "Just got back from the market—everything’s running normal, even the new bus route extension. Friend said the book I wanted was “just sitting there,” so I took it. Nothing’s changed, really. Things are quiet."
Sender 2: "Just heard the new bread rationing system is being tested in the north districts — apparently smooth, no complaints. Funny how things that used to be noisy now just… quiet. You know how it is."
Sender 3: "The quiet has gotten louder — people are moving, things are shifting under the surface, and the usual signs of stability feel like a performance. Whatever’s coming, it’s not just rumor. Keep your heads down, but stay sharp."
Sender 4: "The weather’s been strange this week — hot one day, cold the next — but the garden’s doing fine, and the tomatoes are ripening early. Just keep the windows closed at night, like we talked about."
Sender 5: "The air feels heavier lately — even the quiet ones seem to be holding their breath. Just exchanged a few words with someone who mentioned the new buildings going up and the sudden silence around certain names; it’s like the whole city’s been recalibrated, and we’re all just trying to remember how to move in sync."
Sender 6: "The air feels different — not loud, but heavy. People are quieter, but not afraid. Just… waiting. The system’s still moving, but the gears are grinding. Let’s keep our heads down, but stay sharp."
Sender 7: "The quiet moments lately — the pauses, the looks — they mean something. But the system’s still moving, and the people we trust are just… waiting. Stay sharp, stay close, but don’t reach."
Sender 8: "The air feels different now — people are settling in, making plans, rebuilding. Even the quiet ones seem to have stopped holding their breath. Whatever’s coming, it’s not going to be from the streets."
Sender 9: "Just got word from a few trusted sources — things seem quiet on the surface, but the quiet feels deliberate. People are fixing up their homes, money’s flowing normal, and even the foreign reporters are drifting back in. Feels like everyone’s waiting to see who blinks first."
Sender 10: "Just got back from the market—seems like the usual routine, no signs of anything brewing. The bread’s still the same, and even the old man at the stall said the news feels quiet lately. Guess the system’s just… breathing. Nothing to worry about, but maybe keep the jokes light—some things don’t need saying out loud."

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 10 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 10.
